subject: Preflight: Dedicated GPU runbook & traffic profile — NeuraMetrics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex King <alex.king@neurametrics.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: Dedicated GPU runbook & traffic profile — NeuraMetrics

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call earlier — excited to help map a Dedicated plan for NeuraMetrics. To get a robust preliminary sizing (and suggest a GPU mix + KV cache strategy), can you please send a short traffic profile and one or two sample request traces? The things that move the needle for our sizing model are below; a quick CSV or bullet answers are perfect.

Request: please reply with the following if possible (or attach a sample CSV):
- Peak QPS (requests/sec) and sustained QPS (1h average)
- Typical prompt token length (median + 95th percentile) and typical response token length (median + 95th)
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming
- Session characteristics: fraction of requests that re-use KV cache / have long-lived sessions, avg session duration
- Batchability: are requests independent or can you batch multiple in one call? desired max batching window (ms)
- Latency SLO targets (e.g., p50/p95/p99 per-model) and any tail requirements
- Expected growth over 3 months (e.g., +30% month-over-month)
- Any models you plan to serve (open model name / size), and whether you plan to use quantized variants

If you already have token_samples or burst logs, please attach — those help us run a quick microbenchmark. I attached a small CSV template (Token sample columns: request_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, timestamp) to speed things up.

If it helps, I can also spin up a 30-minute sizing workshop with Marissa and Ben to walk through the profile and deliver a preliminary fleet sketch.

Goal: once we have the profile, we’ll provide a 1–2 page runbook: recommended GPU SKUs, expected occupancy, KV cache sizing, and a delta plan for burst handling.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Alex King <alex.king@neurametrics.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: Dedicated GPU runbook & traffic profile — NeuraMetrics

Hi Aditya,

Thanks — attaching the CSV and a small burst log export. Answers below (high level) — let me know if you want raw traces.

- Peak QPS: 220 req/s (observed during product launch week)
- Sustained QPS (30d average): 48 req/s
- Prompt token length: median 120 tokens, p95 760 tokens
- Response token length: median 90 tokens, p95 1,100 tokens
- Streaming: ~18% of requests use streaming (real-time transcripts), rest are non-streaming
- Sessions: ~26% of requests reuse session KV cache (average session length ~12 minutes)
- Batchability: requests are largely single-shot; small internal batch attempts possible but not reliable. No more than 2 requests per batch; we prefer single request latency.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 650ms for interactive endpoints, p99 <= 1.8s (we can tolerate occasional slowdowns during bursts)
- Growth: expecting +40% QoQ for the next 3 quarters (seasonal product cycle)
- Models: currently using a fine-tuned 13B open model (non-quantized in prod). We are evaluating 8-bit quantized variants for cost.

Attachments: NeuraMetrics_Token_Samples.csv, prod_burst_logs_202506.zip, NeuraMetrics_DPA.pdf

Notes: the burst log contains a 2-hour spike where QPS hit 220; sustained day-to-day traffic is closer to the 40–60 req/s window. If you need synthetic workloads to match p95 response tokens, say so and we’ll generate a labeled sample.

Best,
Alex King
Head of Platform — NeuraMetrics
alex.king@neurametrics.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Preflight: Dedicated GPU runbook & traffic profile — NeuraMetrics

Forwarding NeuraMetrics' traffic export — they included token samples and a short burst log. High-level takeaways: peak 220 qps, sustained ~48 qps, p95 response tokens ~1100, ~26% session affinity (reuses KV). About 18% streaming. They run a tuned 13B model (non-quantized today) and are considering 8-bit. Growth profile strong (+40% QoQ).

Can we run a quick preliminary sizing (sketch) and recommend:
- GPU SKU mix (e.g., how many A10s / H100-equivalents or a hybrid mix)
- KV cache sizing and suggested node footprint for session reuse
- Burst handling strategy (reserve vs. autoscale + fallback model variants)
- Cost ballpark for a monthly Dedicated commitment (committed capacity tier + burst buffer)

Deadline: NeuraMetrics wants a short runbook before next Tue (2025-06-24) so they can prep procurement. Alex is open to a 30-minute review workshop. I can join the call.

Original message below.

Thanks for the forward, Aditya — good profile. Quick clarifying Qs before Ben and I draft the 1–2 page runbook:

1) How often do their long (p95 ~1100 token) responses occur during a burst window? Are p95s evenly distributed or concentrated to a subset of requests?
2) Can they provide a small set (5–10) of representative prompts that produce p95 responses so we can run end-to-end microbenchmarks against quantized vs non-quantized builds?
3) Do they expect the 26% session-affinity traffic to be uniformly distributed across users or concentrated to heavy users? This impacts KV cache sharding.

Plan: Ben — can you run a quick cost sketch with two flavors: (A) conservative Dedicated commit sized for 220 peak with small burst buffer, (B) hybrid: smaller commit sized for 60 sustained with autoscale for peak + fallback to 8-bit model? I’ll draft the runbook text and recommended KV sizing.

Delivery: I can have the draft runbook and cost sketch ready by EOD Monday (2025-06-23) if they can send the 5–10 sample prompts (Alex). We should offer a 30-minute review slot on Tue (2025-06-24) 10:00–10:30 PT (I’ll propose to Alex).
